title.narrative: People provided with access to improved water sources

comment.narrative: Target achieved (127%). RUWASA provided 11,253,162 people from 136 rural districts, with access to improved water sources. Beneficiaries gained access to new, extended, or rehabilitated water points in the form of a household water connection, a public tap, or a standpipe. This indicator's wording was slightly revised, the target was increased from 3,000,000 to 10,137,353, the 50 percent female target was replaced with a number, and a rural breakdown target was added in the December 2022 AF. The target and breakdown female target were then reduced to 8,852,712 and 4,426,356 in the December 2023 restructuring. Information source: IVA reports, the client's completion report, and the RSDMS.

title.narrative: Number of participating district councils submitting accurate and complete sector M&E data

comment.narrative: Target partially achieved (28%-86%). A total of 118 district councils submitted monthly water supply reports to RUWASA using the RSDMS, 67 district councils submitted quarterly household sanitation reports to the regions and then to MoH and PO-RALG through the NSMIS, and 38 district councils submitted annual school sanitation reports to PO-RALG using the BEMIS. This indicator's target was increased from 86 to 137 and its breakdown indicators were added in the December 2022 AF. A total target is not reported as different LGAs complied with different data categories. Information source: IVA reports and the client's completion report.

title.narrative: Number of villages that achieve and sustain community-wide sanitation

comment.narrative: Target partially achieved (63%). A total of 1,105 villages achieved and sustained a community-wide sanitation status at closing. This meant that at least 25 percent (until 2024) or 50 percent (in 2024-2025) of villages households had access to an improved sanitation facility and a handwashing facility, all their public primary schools had improved sanitation and handwashing facilities, and they were free of open defecation. These were sustained by the time of program closed as confirmed by repeat visits of the IVA. This indicator's target was increased from 1,250 to 1,746 in the December 2022 AF. Information source: IVA reports, client's completion report, and the NSMIS.

title.narrative: Number of public primary schools with access to improved sanitation and hygiene facilities

comment.narrative: Target substantially achieved (99%). The government provided 1,830 public primary schools in all 137 districts with access to improved sanitation and hygiene facilities as per requirements in terms of water source, drop hole -student rations, separate facilities for boys, girls, and staff with additional considerations for people with disabilities, and more. Each school designated an active menstrual counsellor, and some introduced ash pits, laundry facilities, fences, waste bins, solar panels, and wastewater treatment systems to further improve hygienic conditions. This indicator's target was increased from 1,500 to 1,853 in the December 2022 AF. Information source: World Bank reports, the client's completion report, and the BEMIS.

title.narrative: Percentage of CBWSO with female members in leadership positions

comment.narrative: Target achieved (105%). All of Tanzania's CBWSOs organizing bodies included females in at least one leadership position - chairperson, treasurer, or vice-chairperson, as per the CBWSO formation guidelines. This indicator's target was changed from 3,667 CBWSOs to 95 percent of the CBWSOs in the December 2022 AF. Information source: World Bank reports, the client's completion report, and monthly check-ups by RUWASA.

title.narrative: People provided with access to improved sanitation services

comment.narrative: Target achieved (137%). The government provided 12,351,280 people from 130 districts with access to improved sanitation services thanks to the construction and repair of improved community, school, and HCF sanitation facilities, such as flush/pour flush toilets, ventilated improved pit latrines, and composting toilets. This indicator's wording was slightly revised, its target was increased from 4,000,000 to 9,040,260, and the female beneficiary target changed from 50% to 4,520,130 in the December 2022 AF. Information source: IVA reports, client's completion report, and the NSMIS.

title.narrative: Number of villages served by a CBWSO with improved O&M capacity for water supply services

comment.narrative: Target achieved (139%). A total of 12,590 villages across 136 districts were served by CBWSOs at closing with improved O&M capacity for water supply services. All the CBWSOs were registered, had in place an active management team, participated in at least one semi-annual district-level community of practice meeting annually, had a well-maintained cash book, and charged tariffs reflecting energy costs. This indicator was introduced in the December 2022 AF with an 8,127 target. This target was increased to 9,035 in the December 2023 restructuring. Information source: IVA reports, the client's completion report, and the RSDMS.

title.narrative: Number of health care facilities with access to improved sanitation and hygiene facilities

comment.narrative: Target achieved (112%). The government provided 2,957 HCFs in the 137 districts with access to improved sanitation and hygiene facilities. HCFs were provided with new or repaired improved sanitation, hygiene, water supply, and waste management facilities. This indicator's target was increased from 1,500 to 2,636 in the December 2022 AF. Information source: World Bank reports, the client's completion report, and the NSMIS.

title.narrative: Number of district community of practice meetings with citizen engagement

comment.narrative: Target achieved (150%). Community members, such as village chairpersons, ward councilors, village executive officers, and schools and HCF personnel, engaged in at least 653 Community of Practice meetings throughout the lifetime of the program. Information source: Client's completion report.

title.narrative: Enrolment ratio of female students for the Water institute

comment.narrative: Target achieved (109%). The female student enrolment ratio for the Water Institute increased from 28 percent to 38 percent during the program thanks to sensitization by the Water Institute in secondary schools. Information source: World Bank reports, the client's completion report, and RUWASA.

title.narrative: Number of sustainably functioning water points

comment.narrative: Target achieved (104%). A total of 83,202 water points functioned sustainably, i.e., they were managed by registered CBWSOs that charged cost-reflective tariffs and were functioning at closing. This indicator's target was increased from 43,811 to 80,000 in the December 2022 AF. Information source: IVA reports, the client's completion report, and the RSDMS.

title.narrative: Increase in access to handwashing facilities among the target population

comment.narrative: Target substantially achieved (90%). There was a 44.8 percent increase in the target population's access to handwashing facilities thanks to the BCC campaign that created demand for handwashing facilities and the HCF, school, and community handwashing facilities established. The result reflects the national average of households with handwashing facilities as verified by community health workers. This indicator's target was increased from 30 percent to 50 percent in the December 2022 AF. Information source: World Bank reports, the client's completion report, and the NSMIS.

Target partially achieved (50%). The milestones were: (i) establishment of RUWASA, (ii) operationalization of RUWASA's audit unit and QA&QC mechanisms, (iii) provision of technical support to 10 percent of CBWSOs, (iv) provision of technical support to 30 percent of CBWSOs, (v) provision of technical support to 50 percent of CBWSOs, and (vi) use of at least 5 percent of RUWASA's annual budget for O&M of water supply facilities in FY23-FY24. This indicator's target was changed from “Agency established” to the achievement of 12 milestones in the December 2022 AF. Information source: World Bank reports, the client's completion report, and RUWASA.
